questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Acceleration due to gravity is different at different places on the surface of earth.
Statement II: Acceleration due to gravity increases as we go down below the earth's surface.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
questions.solution: Statement I is true because the acceleration due to gravity varies with latitude ($g' = g - \omega^2 R \cos^2 \theta$) and due to the non-spherical shape of the Earth. Statement II is false because below the Earth's surface at depth $d$, $g' = g\left(1 - \frac{d}{R}\right)$, which decreases as depth increases.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: If earth has a mass nine times and radius twice to that of a planet P. Then $\frac{v_e}{3}\sqrt{x}\text{ ms}^{-1}$ will be the minimum velocity required by a rocket to pull out of gravitational force of P, where $v_e$ is escape velocity on earth. The value of $x$ is
questions.solution:
Escape velocity is $v_e = \sqrt{\frac{2GM}{R}}$.
For planet P, $M_P = \frac{M}{9}$ and $R_P = \frac{R}{2}$.
Escape velocity from planet P is $v_P = \sqrt{\frac{2GM_P}{R_P}} = \sqrt{\frac{2G(M/9)}{R/2}} = \sqrt{\frac{2}{9}}\sqrt{\frac{2GM}{R}} = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{3} v_e$.
Comparing $v_P = \frac{v_e}{3}\sqrt{x}$, we get $x = 2$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A block of mass $5\text{ kg}$ is placed at rest on a table of rough surface. Now, if a force of $30\text{ N}$ is applied in the direction parallel to surface of the table, the block slides through a distance of $50\text{ m}$ in an interval of time $10\text{ s}$. Coefficient of kinetic friction is (given, $g = 10\text{ ms}^{-2}$):
questions.solution:
From kinematics, $s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2 \implies 50 = 0 + \frac{1}{2}a(10)^2 \implies a = 1\text{ m/s}^2$.
Equation of motion for the block: $F - f_k = ma \implies F - \mu_k mg = ma$.
Substituting values: $30 - \mu_k(5)(10) = 5(1) \implies 30 - 50\mu_k = 5 \implies 50\mu_k = 25 \implies \mu_k = 0.50$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A proton moving with one tenth of velocity of light has a certain de Broglie wavelength of $\lambda$. An alpha particle having certain kinetic energy has the same de-Broglie wavelength $\lambda$. The ratio of kinetic energy of proton and that of alpha particle is:
questions.solution:
de-Broglie wavelength $\lambda = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2mK}}$, so kinetic energy $K = \frac{h^2}{2m\lambda^2}$.
Since $\lambda$ is the same for both, $K \propto \frac{1}{m}$.
Therefore, $\frac{K_p}{K_\alpha} = \frac{m_\alpha}{m_p} = \frac{4m_p}{m_p} = \frac{4}{1}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A steel wire with mass per unit length $7.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ kg m}^{-1}$ is under tension of $70\text{ N}$. The speed of transverse waves in the wire will be:
questions.solution:
The speed of transverse wave on a stretched string is $v = \sqrt{\frac{T}{\mu}}$.
Given $T = 70\text{ N}$ and $\mu = 7.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ kg/m}$.
$v = \sqrt{\frac{70}{7.0 \times 10^{-3}}} = \sqrt{10^4} = 100\text{ m/s}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The average kinetic energy of a molecule of the gas is
options: dependent on the nature of the gas
questions.solution: The average kinetic energy per molecule of an ideal gas is given by $E_k = \frac{f}{2} k_B T$, which is directly proportional to absolute temperature $T$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
Match List I with List II:
List I:
A. Intrinsic semiconductor
B. n-type semiconductor
C. p-type semiconductor
D. Metals
List II:
I. Fermi-level near the valence band
II. Fermi-level in the middle of valence and conduction band.
III. Fermi-level near the conduction band
IV. Fermi-level inside the conduction band
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
1. Intrinsic semiconductor: Fermi-level lies in the middle of the energy gap (A-II).
2. n-type semiconductor: Fermi-level lies near the conduction band (B-III).
3. p-type semiconductor: Fermi-level lies near the valence band (C-I).
4. Metals: Fermi-level lies inside the conduction band (D-IV).
Hence, A-II, B-III, C-I, D-IV.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A child stands on the edge of the cliff $10\text{ m}$ above the ground and throws a stone horizontally with an initial speed of $5\text{ ms}^{-1}$. Neglecting the air resistance, the speed with which the stone hits the ground will be $\underline{\hspace{0.5in}}\text{ ms}^{-1}$ (given, $g = 10\text{ ms}^{-2}$).
questions.solution:
Horizontal component of velocity $v_x = u = 5\text{ m/s}$.
Vertical component of velocity $v_y = \sqrt{2gh} = \sqrt{2 \times 10 \times 10} = \sqrt{200} = 10\sqrt{2}\text{ m/s}$.
Net velocity $v = \sqrt{v_x^2 + v_y^2} = \sqrt{5^2 + 200} = \sqrt{225} = 15\text{ m/s}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Find the magnetic field at the point P in figure. The curved portion is a semicircle connected to two long straight wires.
questions.solution:
The magnetic field at point P is due to:
1) Semi-infinite straight top wire: $B_1 = \frac{\mu_0 i}{4\pi r}$
2) Semicircular loop: $B_2 = \frac{\mu_0 i}{4r}$
3) Lower straight wire along the line passing through P: $B_3 = 0$
Total magnetic field $B = B_1 + B_2 = \frac{\mu_0 i}{4r} + \frac{\mu_0 i}{4\pi r} = \frac{\mu_0 i}{2r}\left(\frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{2\pi}\right)$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Which of the following frequencies does not belong to FM broadcast.
questions.solution: Standard FM broadcasting frequency band ranges from 88 MHz to 108 MHz. Therefore, 64 MHz does not belong to FM broadcast.
